clue.text: Prepare a hint, cryptically, for person sure to succeed

indicators.note: read cryptically, the three words are to be taken apart and their letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to give a broad hint to someone who is bound to take over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptically' signals that PREPARE A HINT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The next in line to a throne or title, whose inheritance is certain, is the heir apparent.

clue.text: Volunteer troops made rough manoeuvres

indicators.note: military manoeuvres move units about, so the letters before are shifted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers put on a rough exercise in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' looks like a noun the troops made, but it is the anagram signal on MADE ROUGH. The Home Guard was Britain's volunteer defence force in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Guard was a wartime part-time defence militia of volunteers too old or exempt for regular service.

clue.text: Keen on including right opening for piece of music

indicators.note: the phrase for keen takes the abbreviation for right inside it

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone fond of a piece of music, especially its opening bars.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the short introductory passage at the start of a song or track.

clue.text: Allowed to go topless, which is shocking

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, the first letter, of the word for allowed

parts.note: something allowed by law is lawful

explanation.surface: A newspaper-style fuss about being permitted to bare all in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go topless' drops the first letter, L, from LAWFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and shocking are synonyms for something dreadfully bad.

clue.text: Game or chat show host on the BBC

definitions.text: chat show host on the BBC
definitions.meaning: Alan ..., Steve Coogan's comic creation, hosted a spoof BBC chat show

explanation.surface: Asking whether a chat show host is up for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Partridge is a fictional, hapless British broadcaster played by Steve Coogan, whose show 'Knowing Me, Knowing You' aired on the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: A partridge is a bird shot for sport, so it is game; Alan Partridge is the famous fictional talk-show presenter.

clue.text: This obstacle will certainly be in the way!

definitions.text: This obstacle will certainly be in the way!

parts.words: This obstacle will certainly be in the way!
parts.note: an obstruction literally placed in the road, so 'in the way' is true in both senses

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark about some obstacle blocking progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the way' means both obstructive and physically on the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier set across a road by police or protesters stops traffic, an obstacle on the route.

clue.text: Approaches both Poles, eating a bit of corn

indicators.note: the two pole letters take the bit of corn into their middle as if swallowing it

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
an ear is the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant

explanation.surface: An explorer heading for both ends of the earth, snacking on corn on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to come close to it, the same as to approach it.

clue.text: One's first address — cheap semi with end collapsing

indicators.note: a building that collapses ends up in a jumble, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's first home, a cheap semi-detached house with one end falling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' suggests a home, which the semi supports; it is a speech. 'collapsing' rearranges CHEAP SEMI END. A semi is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden speech is the first one a new member gives in Parliament, their first formal address.

clue.text: Confess and allow access

definitions.meaning: to ... a fault is to confess it

explanation.definitionFit: Admit has two senses: owning up to something and letting someone enter.

clue.text: Danger signal — Capone has gun around!

indicators.note: the word for gun is placed around the gangster's first name

parts.note: a gun is a firearm
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A warning that the gangster Capone is armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' has the gun word open up to hold the gangster's first name; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire alarm is a bell or siren warning that a building is ablaze.

clue.text: Mouse thanks monarch for making fun of him, say

parts.note: Mickey Mouse, the Disney cartoon character
ta is informal British for thanks
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: Mickey Mouse thanking a king, who was only teasing him.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the mickey is British slang for teasing; 'him, say' points back to Mickey himself as an example of the victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey-taking is British slang for teasing or mocking someone, making fun of them.

clue.text: What indicates a priest is good company, in the money in America

indicators.note: good company is set inside the American currency word

parts.note: the dollar is the currency of the USA

explanation.surface: A priest who is good fun and also wealthy in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good company' looks like praise of the priest; it is G + CO, placed in DOLLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff white clerical collar worn by clergy marks the wearer out as a priest.

clue.text: Arts degree thus suitable for beginners

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: An arts degree that is therefore suited to novices.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic material is elementary, the level fit for those just starting out.

clue.text: Indian side in arena with band playing

indicators.note: a band playing is in motion, and so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports team from India taking the field to music from a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian side' suggests a cricket team, but it is a side dish. 'playing' rearranges ARENA BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a flatbread served alongside curries, a side dish in Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Kid's father?

parts.note: a kid is a young goat, so its father is the male goat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child; here it is a young goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A billy goat is a male goat, which would sire the young goats called kids.

clue.text: M&S bras are designed to create discomfort

indicators.note: something designed is put together in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Marks and Spencer, the British store, abbreviated; its letters M and S are used
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Underwear from Marks and Spencer made deliberately uncomfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges M, S, BRAS and ARE. M&S is Marks and Spencer, a British department store famous for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To embarrass someone is to make them feel awkward and uncomfortable.

clue.text: Venerable figure stripped off soldier

indicators.note: the word is stripped of its outer layer, leaving everything but its two end letters

explanation.surface: An elderly old soldier taking his clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped off' removes S and R from SOLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal word for an old person, one who is venerable through age.

clue.text: Little drink, at first, for writer

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits
1ST, first, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A writer having a little drink first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' looks like 'initially', but AT is used as written and first is 1ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist writes plays, so is a kind of writer.

clue.text: Exercise in school with boy about to ride a bike

parts.note: PE is physical education, the school subject

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for boy is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A school PE lesson in which a boy is about to cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'about to ride' in the surface, but it reverses the boy; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedal is to work a bicycle's pedals, which is how one rides it.

clue.text: Holiday firm's fare early in the day

parts.note: a short holiday is a break
fast means firmly fixed, as in held fast

explanation.surface: A holiday company's menu for the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holiday firm' reads as a travel company; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast is the first meal of the day, food eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Initial appearance when trying clothes

indicators.note: the two words clothe the answer, which sits inside them across the gap

explanation.surface: Someone's first look in a mirror while trying on clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like garments but is a verb: the words clothe the answer. The definition picks the sense of an entrance on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is the act of coming in, a first appearance on stage or in a scene.

clue.text: Somewhat past it, learned doctor or professor?

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An academic who is rather past their best yet still learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor and professor are forms of address used before a name, as is a title like Mr or Lady.

clue.text: Rely on chauffeur taking day off in waterside area

indicators.note: the day abbreviation comes off the word for chauffeur

parts.note: a chauffeur is a driver
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: Depending on one's chauffeur, who is having a day off by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' (with 'taking' as link) removes the day letter from the chauffeur word; the 'Rely on' piece goes last even though it is printed first.
explanation.definitionFit: A riverbank is the land along the edge of a river, an area beside the water.

clue.text: One's played a role in Twelfth Night

definitions.meaning: a stringed instrument, one that is played
The heroine of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: An actor who has taken a part in Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played a role' looks like one phrase about acting; the split comes after 'played'.
explanation.definitionFit: A viola is a stringed instrument bowed by musicians; Viola is the disguised heroine of Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Stir up arguments, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for arguments is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: rows, rhyming with cows, are noisy arguments

explanation.surface: Stirring up quarrels, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: ROWS here rhymes with 'cows', not 'goes'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to stir up or provoke, as in rousing a crowd.

clue.text: Oat fancy after stew is something hard to handle

indicators.note: the rearranged oats come after the stew in the answer

parts.note: a hotpot is a meat and potato stew

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine freely, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fancy oats served after a stew, a tricky dish to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges OAT into OTATO; HOTPOT is a Lancashire stew of meat under sliced potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a controversial issue nobody wants to deal with.

clue.text: Place to learn about a kind of rugby

parts.note: uni is short for university
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A college that teaches about a form of rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby union is the fifteen-a-side form of rugby football, distinct from rugby league.

clue.text: Mark and John are here, in Tyneside area with Will

parts.note: NE is North East England, where Tyneside lies
a testament is a will, as in last will and testament

explanation.surface: Two men called Mark and John live near Newcastle with a third named Will.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark and John look like men's names, as does Will; they are Gospels. Tyneside is the Newcastle area of North East England.
explanation.definitionFit: The gospels of Mark and John are books contained in the second part of the Christian Bible.
